title: CMS console Notification Center (M)
description:
One place in the CMS console for everything a human might need to see or act on. Approach (Ryan): explore by building it and using it. Smallest first version: a page listing open review requests (hard gates and soft reviews from the human review points story) and Cyclotron items routed to humans, with approve, reject and feedback controls, per-user unread/read, and the ordering below. The auto-decided monitor stream, corrections feeding ground truth, and the email digest follow. First slices are built and tried on Distinctive's TTAB flow.

Combines:
1. Cyclotron items routed to humans for review because classifier confidence was low. Featured: most prominent and actionable. Unify the existing curation, monitoring and relevance-decision review surfaces rather than duplicating them. Starting points: src/papyrus_content/relevance_decisions.py, monitoring_router.py / monitoring_routing.py, relevance_recording.py, relevance_sweep.py and the curation code in the console.
2. A monitor stream of recent Cyclotron classifications that were NOT routed to humans (auto-decided on confidence). Filterable by publication, label and confidence. A human can correct one, which feeds back as a ground-truth label.
3. Review requests from the human review points story (PPY-ab6a50): hard gates, soft reviews, flags.

Ordering: hard gates; soft reviews close to their deadline; Cyclotron reviews; flags; then the auto-decided stream.

Each entry links to the item with enough context to decide, and has approve, reject, feedback and correct controls as appropriate. Per-user unread and read state. An email digest for editors; Slack optional later. Who receives notifications and the digest is per-site configuration, per review mode and/or per automation: a list of editor or admin users plus optional extra email recipients, defaulting to the site owner, changeable without a code change.

Acceptance criteria:
- Entries appear in the stated order and each links to its item with decision context.
- Low-confidence Cyclotron items are featured and actionable; the existing review surfaces are replaced by, not duplicated beside, this page.
- The auto-decided stream filters by publication, label and confidence; correcting an entry records a ground-truth label.
- Approve, reject, feedback and correct work where applicable and are limited to editors and admins; read/unread is tracked per user.
- The email digest goes to the configured recipients; recipients are changeable in configuration without a code change and default to the site owner.
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) required.

Depends on the human review points story (PPY-ab6a50). Distinctive Mark is the test site.

Product direction (Ryan, 2026-10-23): the Notification Center is the CMS console home, the first thing an editor sees after sign-in. Interacting selectively with a stream of review and steering opportunities, and ignoring some of them and letting them run, is the primary editor experience on sites with private backends. If you only look, the system keeps doing what it is doing; if you steer, it incorporates that steering as it moves forward. Everything except hard gates is ignore-safe. See docs/notification-center.md.

Notification Center is the console home (Overview tab): summary line, hard gates, soft reviews by deadline, Cyclotron held items (list + deep links into the existing References review), flags, answered-and-applied steering, collapsible read-only auto-decided stream, per-user read state, words and marks. Remains: embed or replace the References review surface, stream filters (publication, label, confidence), correction to ground truth, email digest. Docs: docs/notification-center.md. Left in_progress.
